sections.body: Feelings have names: excited, nervous, frustrated, jealous, proud, lonely.
Naming a feeling helps it shrink: 'I feel frustrated because my drawing went wrong.'
Calm-down tools: smell the flower, blow the candle (slow breaths), count to 10, squeeze a pillow, ask for a hug.
Practise 'flower and candle' breathing: breathe in through your nose like smelling a flower, then blow out slowly like a candle.
Practise calm-down tools when your child is calm, so they're easier to use when upset.

quiz.q: You feel nervous before a race. Which tool helps?
hints: Slow breathing helps your heart slow down.
When you feel cross, counting to 10 helps. Which calm-down tool is here?
quiz.explain: Slow breaths calm your body down.

quiz.q: Your brother broke your toy. You feel angry. What helps first?
options: Say how you feel: 'I'm angry because…'
hints: 'I'm sad because I lost my ball' tells people what's wrong. Use words the same way.
quiz.explain: Naming the feeling with words helps, and then you can sort it out together.
